record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: If a neighbourhood of the boundary of the billiard table Ω ⊂ R2 is foliated by caustics, then the billiard curve γ is an ellipse. We also formulate a generalized conjecture: if an open subset of the convex billiard table is foliated by caustics, then this table is elliptic. A polynomial version of Birkhoff's conjecture concerns the case wh en the integral of the billiard map is polynomial in the velocity. In the case of outer billiards, one modifies t hese conjectures in an obvious way (since outer billiards are affine-equivariant, there is no differenc e between ellipses and circles, and circles are integrable due to symmetry). The state of the art of the (smooth) Birkhoff conjecture is as follo ws. The special case of the conjecture in which the caustics of the billiard trajectories foliate Ω, except for one point, was proved by M. Bialy [13]; later he extended this result to the elliptic and hyperbolic planes [1 6]. Bialy also proved a version of this result for magnetic billiards in constant magnetic field on surfa ces of constant curvature [14]. Recently, substantial progress toward Birkhoff's conjecture was made by V. Kaloshin and his co-authors [5, 127, 117]: they proved the Birkhoff conjecture for small pertu rbations of ellipses. The general case remains open, and it is one of the foremost problems in this field.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝ² be a strictly convex planar domain with smooth boundary γ. The (Birkhoff) billiard in Ω is the dynamical system describing the free motion of a point particle inside Ω that reflects off γ according to the law "angle of incidence equals angle of reflection." A smooth closed curve Γ ⊂ Ω is called a caustic of the billiard if every billiard trajectory tangent to Γ remains tangent to Γ after each reflection off γ.

Conjecture (Birkhoff): If there exists an open neighbourhood U of γ inside Ω such that U \ γ is foliated by caustics of the billiard in Ω, then γ is an ellipse.

Prove or disprove this conjecture. Also consider the generalized form: if some open subset of Ω is foliated by caustics of the billiard, must γ be an ellipse?
artifact.status_search_result: The smooth Birkhoff conjecture remains open in full generality. Major partial progress includes Bialy's theorem (boundary foliated except possibly one point), the local version proved by Avila–De Simoi–Kaloshin and Kaloshin–Sorrentino (small perturbations of ellipses must be ellipses), and complete proofs of the polynomial version by Bialy–Mironov and Glutsyuk. New integrable examples (e.g., billiards inside cones, 2025) suggest the landscape is still being mapped, but the original conjecture for general smooth convex tables is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the local Birkhoff conjecture for convex billiards
status_evidence.snippet: A small integrable perturbation of an ellipse must be an ellipse.
status_evidence.claim: Local Birkhoff conjecture is proved; global case remains open.

status_evidence.title: On polynomially integrable Birkhoff billiards on surfaces of constant curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial version of the Birkhoff conjecture resolved.

status_evidence.title: Integrable Birkhoff Billiards inside Cones
status_evidence.snippet: New integrable billiard examples beyond quadrics (2025).
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues; general conjecture not closed.
